generatedCommentsNodes.comment: In `IngestStats.ByteStats.toXContent`, the condition `if (bytesIngested > 0 && bytesProduced > 0)` prevents either metric from being reported if one of them is zero. For example, if a pipeline ingests data but drops all documents (resulting in `bytesProduced == 0`), neither the ingested nor produced byte counts will be visible in the API response. This logic should likely use a logical OR (`||`) or check each field independently to ensure that any non-zero activity is reported.

The `peekFirst()` method identifies the "first" pipeline using `defaultPipeline != null ? defaultPipeline : finalPipeline`. If these fields only represent index-level settings, this logic may fail to identify a pipeline explicitly specified in the request as the first pipeline. While it is unclear from this chapter how `defaultPipeline` is populated, typically the resolution order for ingest pipelines is: *Request Pipeline* $\rightarrow$ *Default Pipeline* $\rightarrow$ *Final Pipeline*. If `defaultPipeline` does not encompass the request-specified pipeline, stats will be attributed to the wrong pipeline or missed entirely.

Figured out what was wrong - when the stats of a pipeline gets updated via another pipeline's stats it wasn't updating the `IngestPipelineMetric` stats, so I fixed that and changed some of the tests as necessary

As an aside, I was at first very confused about why the `endSize1` was increasing despite the failure. Also why the `_id1` pipeline has a `failed` count of 0 in the ` assertPipelineStats` call above. When there is an on_failure processor, the resulting document does get sent to the index, so that explains why it is in the bytesProduced stat. (You may have been aware of all this already).
